# Lichess Chess Game Analytics Report

## Overview

You are tasked with producing a comprehensive analytical report on over 20,000 Lichess chess games. The report — **"Lichess Chess Game Analytics: Patterns of Victory, Openings, and Player Dynamics"** — should give the reader a thorough, data-driven understanding of the factors that influence game outcomes on the platform: color advantage, rating dynamics, opening choices, time controls, and how these dimensions interact.

The target audience is **analysts** — people comfortable with statistics, charts, and detailed breakdowns. The tone should be **analytical, detailed, and data-forward**: lead with numbers, support claims with visualizations, and avoid vague generalizations. Every figure cited must come directly from `data.csv`.

## Key Priorities

- **The "White vs. Black: First-Move Advantage" section is the centerpiece.** Quantify white's edge precisely, break it down by rating bracket and time control, and make it visually compelling. This is the question every chess audience cares about most.
- **Rating Differential Impact** is the most analytically interesting KPI — go beyond a simple correlation number. Show how win probability shifts across different rating gaps, ideally with a binned chart.
- **Opening analysis** should focus on the top 10–15 openings by frequency. Don't try to cover every ECO code — depth over breadth. Highlight any openings where black actually outperforms white.
- Ensure the **Key Findings** section is a tight, actionable synthesis — not a repetition of prior sections. A coach or platform analyst should be able to read just that section and walk away informed.

## Data Integrity

**Absolutely no fabrication.** Every statistic, percentage, and trend must be derived from `data.csv`. If data is missing or ambiguous for a particular analysis, note the limitation rather than inventing numbers.

## Output

Deliver the final report as **`/app/output/final_report.html`**. Use clean, professional styling with embedded charts suitable for browser viewing.

Refer to `task_input.json` for the full specification of required sections, KPIs, and analysis dimensions.

---

3. Read `/app/benchmark/data.csv` as the primary dataset to analyze.

2. All visualizations must be embedded in the report (inline SVG, base64 images, or chart libraries loaded via CDN).
3. The report must be self-contained — openable directly in a browser (if HTML) or readable as-is (if PDF).

1	# Chess Game Dataset (Lichess)
2	
3	## About the Dataset
4	
5	This dataset contains **20,058 chess games** collected from the online chess platform [Lichess.org](https://lichess.org), sourced from the Kaggle dataset `datasnaek/chess`. The data was gathered via the Lichess API by collecting game histories from users belonging to large Lichess teams. Each row represents a single completed chess game with comprehensive metadata including player information, ratings, game outcome, time controls, full move notation, and opening classification.
6	
7	The dataset has **16 columns** and is stored in a single CSV file (`games.csv`).
8	
9	## Column Schema
10	
11	| Column Name | Type | Description |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| `id` | String | Unique game identifier from Lichess |
14	| `rated` | Boolean | Whether the game was rated (`TRUE`) or casual (`FALSE`). Rated games affect player ratings. |
15	| `created_at` | String | Timestamp (Unix epoch in milliseconds) when the game was created/started. Stored as a floating-point number string (e.g., `1.50421E+12`). |
16	| `last_move_at` | String | Timestamp (Unix epoch in milliseconds) when the last move was made. Same format as `created_at`. |
17	| `turns` | Integer | Total number of half-moves (plies) in the game. A turn by white followed by a turn by black counts as 2 turns. |
18	| `victory_status` | String | How the game ended. Known values include: `mate` (checkmate), `resign` (a player resigned), `outoftime` (a player ran out of time), `draw` (game drawn). |
19	| `winner` | String | The winning side: `white`, `black`, or `draw`. |
20	| `increment_code` | String | Time control in the format `base+increment` (e.g., `15+2` means 15 minutes base time with 2 seconds added per move). |
21	| `white_id` | String | Lichess username of the player with the white pieces. |
22	| `white_rating` | Integer | Elo rating of the white player at the time of the game. |
23	| `black_id` | String | Lichess username of the player with the black pieces. |
24	| `black_rating` | Integer | Elo rating of the black player at the time of the game. |
25	| `moves` | String | Full game move sequence in Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN), space-separated. |
26	| `opening_eco` | String | ECO (Encyclopaedia of Chess Openings) code classifying the opening played (e.g., `D10`, `B00`, `C41`). |
27	| `opening_name` | String | Human-readable name of the opening and variation (e.g., "Slav Defense: Exchange Variation"). |
28	| `opening_ply` | Integer | Number of half-moves (plies) that constitute the opening phase of the game. |
29	
30	## Data Quality Notes
31	
32	- **Timestamps**: The `created_at` and `last_move_at` columns are stored as scientific notation strings representing Unix epoch milliseconds. They require conversion for meaningful time-based analysis.
33	- **Winner field**: When the game is a draw, the `winner` column contains the value `draw` rather than being null or empty.
34	- **Moves column**: Contains the full game notation as a single long string. Parsing individual moves requires splitting on spaces.
35	- **Rating range**: Player ratings span a wide range typical of online chess platforms, from beginners (~800) to strong players (~2700).
36	- **Opening names**: Some opening names include multiple levels of variation separated by colons (e.g., "Slav Defense: Exchange Variation"), which may need parsing for grouped analysis.
37	- **No missing values** are expected in the core columns based on the API source, but the `winner` column may contain `draw` entries that should be handled separately from white/black wins in win-rate calculations.
38	
39	## Context
40	
41	Chess is a game of patterns, and this dataset enables analysis of how factors such as player rating, color assignment, opening choice, and time control influence game outcomes. The data is well-suited for exploring the classic "white advantage" hypothesis, rating-based performance modeling, and opening effectiveness analysis.

This dataset contains **20,058 chess games** collected from the online chess platform [Lichess.org](https://lichess.org), sourced from the Kaggle dataset `datasnaek/chess`. The data was gathered via the Lichess API by collecting game histories from users belonging to large Lichess teams. Each row represents a single completed chess game with comprehensive metadata including player information, ratings, game outcome, time controls, full move notation, and opening classification.

The dataset has **16 columns** and is stored in a single CSV file (`games.csv`).

## Column Schema

| Column Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | String | Unique game identifier from Lichess |
| `rated` | Boolean | Whether the game was rated (`TRUE`) or casual (`FALSE`). Rated games affect player ratings. |
| `created_at` | String | Timestamp (Unix epoch in milliseconds) when the game was created/started. Stored as a floating-point number string (e.g., `1.50421E+12`). |
| `last_move_at` | String | Timestamp (Unix epoch in milliseconds) when the last move was made. Same format as `created_at`. |
| `turns` | Integer | Total number of half-moves (plies) in the game. A turn by white followed by a turn by black counts as 2 turns. |
| `victory_status` | String | How the game ended. Known values include: `mate` (checkmate), `resign` (a player resigned), `outoftime` (a player ran out of time), `draw` (game drawn). |
| `winner` | String | The winning side: `white`, `black`, or `draw`. |
| `increment_code` | String | Time control in the format `base+increment` (e.g., `15+2` means 15 minutes base time with 2 seconds added per move). |
| `white_id` | String | Lichess username of the player with the white pieces. |
| `white_rating` | Integer | Elo rating of the white player at the time of the game. |
| `black_id` | String | Lichess username of the player with the black pieces. |
| `black_rating` | Integer | Elo rating of the black player at the time of the game. |
| `moves` | String | Full game move sequence in Standard Algebraic Notation (SAN), space-separated. |
| `opening_eco` | String | ECO (Encyclopaedia of Chess Openings) code classifying the opening played (e.g., `D10`, `B00`, `C41`). |
| `opening_name` | String | Human-readable name of the opening and variation (e.g., "Slav Defense: Exchange Variation"). |
| `opening_ply` | Integer | Number of half-moves (plies) that constitute the opening phase of the game. |

## Data Quality Notes

- **Timestamps**: The `created_at` and `last_move_at` columns are stored as scientific notation strings representing Unix epoch milliseconds. They require conversion for meaningful time-based analysis.
- **Winner field**: When the game is a draw, the `winner` column contains the value `draw` rather than being null or empty.
- **Moves column**: Contains the full game notation as a single long string. Parsing individual moves requires splitting on spaces.
- **Rating range**: Player ratings span a wide range typical of online chess platforms, from beginners (~800) to strong players (~2700).
- **Opening names**: Some opening names include multiple levels of variation separated by colons (e.g., "Slav Defense: Exchange Variation"), which may need parsing for grouped analysis.
- **No missing values** are expected in the core columns based on the API source, but the `winner` column may contain `draw` entries that should be handled separately from white/black wins in win-rate calculations.

## Context

Chess is a game of patterns, and this dataset enables analysis of how factors such as player rating, color assignment, opening choice, and time control influence game outcomes. The data is well-suited for exploring the classic "white advantage" hypothesis, rating-based performance modeling, and opening effectiveness analysis.

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import json
import math
from collections import Counter

# ── Load data ──
df = pd.read_csv('/app/benchmark/data.csv')
TOTAL_GAMES = len(df)

# Helper
def pct(n, d):
    return (n / d * 100) if d > 0 else 0

# ────────────────────────────────────────────
# SECTION 1: Dataset Overview & Game Distribution
# ────────────────────────────────────────────
rated_count = int(df['rated'].eq(True).sum())
unrated_count = int(df['rated'].eq(False).sum())

victory_dist = df['victory_status'].value_counts().to_dict()
winner_dist = df['winner'].value_counts().to_dict()

# Ensure all expected values
for k in ['mate', 'resign', 'outoftime', 'draw']:
    victory_dist.setdefault(k, 0)
for k in ['white', 'black', 'draw']:
    winner_dist.setdefault(k, 0)

# Decisive vs draw
draw_count = int(winner_dist.get('draw', 0))
decisive_count = int(TOTAL_GAMES - draw_count)

# ────────────────────────────────────────────
# SECTION 2: White vs. Black Advantage (CENTERPIECE)
# ────────────────────────────────────────────
decisive = df[df['winner'] != 'draw']
white_wins = int(decisive[decisive['winner'] == 'white'].shape[0])
black_wins = int(decisive[decisive['winner'] == 'black'].shape[0])
white_win_rate = pct(white_wins, decisive_count)

# White win rate by victory status
ww_by_status = {}
for status in ['mate', 'resign', 'outoftime']:
    subset = decisive[decisive['victory_status'] == status]
    ww = int(subset[subset['winner'] == 'white'].shape[0])
    total = int(subset.shape[0])
    ww_by_status[status] = {'white_wins': ww, 'total': total, 'rate': pct(ww, total)}

# By rating bracket
brackets = [(0, 1200), (1200, 1500), (1500, 1800), (1800, 2100), (2100, 3000)]
bracket_labels = ['<1200', '1200-1500', '1500-1800', '1800-2100', '2100+']

ww_by_bracket = []
for (lo, hi), label in zip(brackets, bracket_labels):
    subset = decisive[(decisive['white_rating'] >= lo) & (decisive['white_rating'] < hi)]
    ww = int(subset[subset['winner'] == 'white'].shape[0])
    total = int(subset.shape[0])
    ww_by_bracket.append({'bracket': label, 'white_wins': ww, 'total': total, 'rate': pct(ww, total)})

# By time control (top categories)
tc_groups = df.groupby('increment_code')
tc_white_win = []
for tc in df['increment_code'].value_counts().head(10).index:
    subset = tc_groups.get_group(tc)
    sub_dec = subset[subset['winner'] != 'draw']
    ww = int(sub_dec[sub_dec['winner'] == 'white'].shape[0])
    total = int(sub_dec.shape[0])
    tc_white_win.append({'time_control': tc, 'white_wins': ww, 'total': total, 'rate': pct(ww, total), 'all_games': int(subset.shape[0])})

# ────────────────────────────────────────────
# SECTION 3: Rating Dynamics
# ────────────────────────────────────────────
white_rating_mean = float(df['white_rating'].mean())
white_rating_median = float(df['white_rating'].median())
white_rating_std = float(df['white_rating'].std())
black_rating_mean = float(df['black_rating'].mean())
black_rating_median = float(df['black_rating'].median())
black_rating_std = float(df['black_rating'].std())

# Rating differential = white - black
df_dec = decisive.copy()
df_dec['rating_diff'] = df_dec['white_rating'] - df_dec['black_rating']
df_dec['white_won'] = (df_dec['winner'] == 'white').astype(int)

# Binned win probability by rating diff
bins = [(-float('inf'), -400), (-400, -300), (-300, -200), (-200, -150), (-150, -100),
        (-100, -50), (-50, 0), (0, 50), (50, 100), (100, 150), (150, 200), (200, 300), (300, 400), (400, float('inf'))]
bin_labels = ['<-400', '-400:-300', '-300:-200', '-200:-150', '-150:-100',
              '-100:-50', '-50:0', '0:+50', '+50:+100', '+100:+150', '+150:+200', '+200:+300', '+300:+400', '>+400']

diff_bins = []
for (lo, hi), label in zip(bins, bin_labels):
    subset = df_dec[(df_dec['rating_diff'] > lo) & (df_dec['rating_diff'] <= hi)]
    ww = int(subset['white_won'].sum())
    total = int(subset.shape[0])
    diff_bins.append({'bin': label, 'white_wins': ww, 'total': total, 'white_win_rate': pct(ww, total)})

# Average turns by rating tier (using white_rating)
avg_turns_by_bracket = []
for (lo, hi), label in zip(brackets, bracket_labels):
    subset = df[df['white_rating'].between(lo, hi - 1)]
    avg_turns_by_bracket.append({
        'bracket': label,
        'avg_turns': float(subset['turns'].mean()),
        'median_turns': float(subset['turns'].median()),
        'games': int(subset.shape[0])
    })

# Overall avg turns by victory status
avg_turns_by_status = {}
for status in ['mate', 'resign', 'outoftime', 'draw']:
    subset = df[df['victory_status'] == status]
    avg_turns_by_status[status] = {
        'avg_turns': float(subset['turns'].mean()),
        'median_turns': float(subset['turns'].median()),
        'count': int(subset.shape[0])
    }

# ────────────────────────────────────────────
# SECTION 4: Opening Analysis
# ────────────────────────────────────────────
# Top openings by frequency
opening_counts = df['opening_name'].value_counts().head(15)
top_openings = []
for op_name, count in opening_counts.items():
    subset = df[df['opening_name'] == op_name]
    sub_dec = subset[subset['winner'] != 'draw']
    ww = int(sub_dec[sub_dec['winner'] == 'white'].shape[0])
    bw = int(sub_dec[sub_dec['winner'] == 'black'].shape[0])
    total_dec = int(sub_dec.shape[0])
    top_openings.append({
        'opening': op_name,
        'eco': subset['opening_eco'].iloc[0],
        'games': int(count),
        'white_wins': ww,
        'black_wins': bw,
        'draws': int(subset[subset['winner'] == 'draw'].shape[0]),
        'white_win_rate': pct(ww, total_dec) if total_dec else 0,
        'black_win_rate': pct(bw, total_dec) if total_dec else 0,
        'avg_ply': float(subset['opening_ply'].mean()),
        'avg_turns': float(subset['turns'].mean())
    })

# ECO distribution
eco_counts = df['opening_eco'].value_counts().head(15)
top_eco = []
for eco, count in eco_counts.items():
    subset = df[df['opening_eco'] == eco]
    sub_dec = subset[subset['winner'] != 'draw']
    ww = int(sub_dec[sub_dec['winner'] == 'white'].shape[0])
    bw = int(sub_dec[sub_dec['winner'] == 'black'].shape[0])
    total_dec = int(sub_dec.shape[0])
    op_names = subset['opening_name'].iloc[0]
    top_eco.append({
        'eco': eco,
        'opening_name': op_names.split(':')[0] if ':' in op_names else op_names,
        'games': int(count),
        'white_wins': ww,
        'black_wins': bw,
        'draws': int(subset[subset['winner'] == 'draw'].shape[0]),
        'white_win_rate': pct(ww, total_dec) if total_dec else 0,
        'black_win_rate': pct(bw, total_dec) if total_dec else 0,
    })

# Openings where black outperforms white
black_better = []
for op in top_openings:
    if op['black_win_rate'] > op['white_win_rate']:
        black_better.append(op)

# Opening ply vs win rate
ply_bins = [(0, 3), (3, 5), (5, 7), (7, 10), (10, 15), (15, 50)]
ply_labels = ['0-2', '3-4', '5-6', '7-9', '10-14', '15+']
ply_analysis = []
for (lo, hi), label in zip(ply_bins, ply_labels):
    subset = df[df['opening_ply'].between(lo, hi - 1 if hi < 50 else hi, inclusive='left')]
    sub_dec = subset[subset['winner'] != 'draw']
    ww = int(sub_dec[sub_dec['winner'] == 'white'].shape[0])
    total = int(sub_dec.shape[0])
    ply_analysis.append({
        'ply_range': label,
        'games': int(subset.shape[0]),
        'white_win_rate': pct(ww, total) if total else 0,
        'draw_rate': pct(int(subset[subset['winner'] == 'draw'].shape[0]), int(subset.shape[0])),
        'avg_turns': float(subset['turns'].mean())
    })

# ────────────────────────────────────────────
# SECTION 5: Time Control Analysis
# ────────────────────────────────────────────
# Group time controls into categories
def classify_tc(tc_str):
    try:
        base, inc = tc_str.split('+')
        base, inc = int(base), int(inc)
    except:
        return 'Other'
    if base <= 3:
        return 'Bullet (≤3min)'
    elif base <= 10:
        return 'Blitz (3-10min)'
    elif base <= 30:
        return 'Rapid (10-30min)'
    else:
        return 'Classical (>30min)'

df['tc_category'] = df['increment_code'].apply(classify_tc)
tc_cat_counts = df['tc_category'].value_counts().to_dict()

tc_cat_analysis = []
for cat in ['Bullet (≤3min)', 'Blitz (3-10min)', 'Rapid (10-30min)', 'Classical (>30min)']:
    subset = df[df['tc_category'] == cat]
    if subset.shape[0] == 0:
        continue
    sub_dec = subset[subset['winner'] != 'draw']
    ww = int(sub_dec[sub_dec['winner'] == 'white'].shape[0])
    total_dec = int(sub_dec.shape[0])

    vs_dist = subset['victory_status'].value_counts().to_dict()
    mate_pct = pct(vs_dist.get('mate', 0), int(subset.shape[0]))
    resign_pct = pct(vs_dist.get('resign', 0), int(subset.shape[0]))
    timeout_pct = pct(vs_dist.get('outoftime', 0), int(subset.shape[0]))
    draw_pct = pct(vs_dist.get('draw', 0), int(subset.shape[0]))

    tc_cat_analysis.append({
        'category': cat,
        'games': int(subset.shape[0]),
        'white_win_rate': pct(ww, total_dec) if total_dec else 0,
        'avg_turns': float(subset['turns'].mean()),
        'median_turns': float(subset['turns'].median()),
        'mate_pct': mate_pct,
        'resign_pct': resign_pct,
        'timeout_pct': timeout_pct,
        'draw_pct': draw_pct
    })

# Top 10 specific time controls
tc_detail = df['increment_code'].value_counts().head(10)
tc_top_detail = []
for tc, count in tc_detail.items():
    subset = df[df['increment_code'] == tc]
    sub_dec = subset[subset['winner'] != 'draw']
    ww = int(sub_dec[sub_dec['winner'] == 'white'].shape[0])
    total_dec = int(sub_dec.shape[0])
    vs_dist = subset['victory_status'].value_counts().to_dict()
    tc_top_detail.append({
        'time_control': tc,
        'games': int(count),
        'white_win_rate': pct(ww, total_dec) if total_dec else 0,
        'avg_turns': float(subset['turns'].mean()),
        'mate_pct': pct(vs_dist.get('mate', 0), int(subset.shape[0])),
        'resign_pct': pct(vs_dist.get('resign', 0), int(subset.shape[0])),
        'timeout_pct': pct(vs_dist.get('outoftime', 0), int(subset.shape[0])),
        'draw_pct': pct(vs_dist.get('draw', 0), int(subset.shape[0])),
    })

# ────────────────────────────────────────────
# SECTION 6: Correlation: rating differential impact
# ────────────────────────────────────────────
from scipy.stats import pearsonr
rating_diff_vals = df_dec['rating_diff'].values
white_won_vals = df_dec['white_won'].values
corr, p_value = pearsonr(rating_diff_vals, white_won_vals)

# Higher-rated player win probability (by absolute diff)
df_dec['abs_diff'] = abs(df_dec['rating_diff'])
df_dec['favored_won'] = ((df_dec['rating_diff'] > 0) & (df_dec['white_won'] == 1)) | \
                         ((df_dec['rating_diff'] < 0) & (df_dec['white_won'] == 0))

# Binned by absolute rating difference
abs_bins = [(0, 25), (25, 50), (50, 100), (100, 150), (150, 200), (200, 300), (300, 400), (400, float('inf'))]
abs_labels = ['0-25', '25-50', '50-100', '100-150', '150-200', '200-300', '300-400', '400+']
abs_diff_analysis = []
for (lo, hi), label in zip(abs_bins, abs_labels):
    subset = df_dec[(df_dec['abs_diff'] > lo) & (df_dec['abs_diff'] <= hi)]
    fw = int(subset['favored_won'].sum())
    total = int(subset.shape[0])
    abs_diff_analysis.append({
        'diff_range': label,
        'favored_wins': fw,
        'total': total,
        'favored_win_rate': pct(fw, total)
    })

# ────────────────────────────────────────────
# Additional: Rating distribution histogram data
# ────────────────────────────────────────────
all_ratings = pd.concat([df['white_rating'], df['black_rating']])
rating_hist_bins = [800, 1000, 1200, 1400, 1600, 1800, 2000, 2200, 2400, 2700]
rating_hist = np.histogram(all_ratings, bins=rating_hist_bins)

# ────────────────────────────────────────────
# ASSEMBLE ALL STATS
# ────────────────────────────────────────────
stats = {
    'total_games': TOTAL_GAMES,
    'rated_count': rated_count,
    'unrated_count': unrated_count,
    'rated_pct': pct(rated_count, TOTAL_GAMES),
    'unrated_pct': pct(unrated_count, TOTAL_GAMES),

    'victory_dist': victory_dist,
    'winner_dist': winner_dist,
    'draw_count': draw_count,
    'decisive_count': decisive_count,
    'draw_pct': pct(draw_count, TOTAL_GAMES),

    # White advantage
    'white_wins': white_wins,
    'black_wins': black_wins,
    'white_win_rate': white_win_rate,
    'ww_by_status': ww_by_status,
    'ww_by_bracket': ww_by_bracket,
    'tc_white_win': tc_white_win,

    # Rating
    'white_rating_mean': white_rating_mean,
    'white_rating_median': white_rating_median,
    'white_rating_std': white_rating_std,
    'black_rating_mean': black_rating_mean,
    'black_rating_median': black_rating_median,
    'black_rating_std': black_rating_std,
    'diff_bins': diff_bins,
    'avg_turns_by_bracket': avg_turns_by_bracket,
    'avg_turns_by_status': avg_turns_by_status,

    # Rating differential impact (higher-rated player wins)
    'correlation': {'r': float(corr), 'p_value': float(p_value)},
    'abs_diff_analysis': abs_diff_analysis,

    # Openings
    'top_openings': top_openings,
    'top_eco': top_eco,
    'black_better_openings': black_better,
    'ply_analysis': ply_analysis,

    # Time controls
    'tc_categories': tc_cat_counts,
    'tc_cat_analysis': tc_cat_analysis,
    'tc_top_detail': tc_top_detail,

    # Rating histogram
    'rating_hist': {'bins': rating_hist_bins, 'counts': rating_hist[0].tolist()},
}

# Write stats JSON
with open('/app/stats.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump(stats, f, indent=2)

print("Analysis complete. Stats written to /app/stats.json")
print(f"Total games: {TOTAL_GAMES}")
print(f"White win rate (decisive): {white_win_rate:.1f}%")
print(f"White wins: {white_wins}, Black wins: {black_wins}, Draws: {draw_count}")

1. Dataset Overview & Game Distribution

The dataset comprises 20,058 chess games collected from Lichess.org. Of these, 16,155 (80.5%) were rated games and 3,903 (19.5%) were casual/unrated. Draws accounted for 950 games (4.7%), leaving 19,108 decisive games for win-rate analysis.

Key takeaway: Resignation is the dominant endgame mechanism (55.6%), reflecting Lichess's culture of players conceding lost positions rather than playing to mate. Only 31.5% of games reach actual checkmate. With draws at just 4.7%, the dataset skews toward decisive outcomes — far lower draw rates than elite classical chess (~30–40%).

2. White vs. Black: The First-Move Advantage

Of the 19,108 decisive games, white won 10,001 (52.3%) and black won 9,107 (47.7%). This 4.7 percentage-point gap confirms a statistically meaningful first-move advantage — white wins approximately 1.10 games for every 1 game black wins.

Notable: Time expiration is the only category where white's edge disappears (49.7%). This likely reflects black's defensive pragmatism in time-scramble positions — protecting their clock while forcing white to prove an advantage. In classical over-the-board chess, white's win rate under time pressure would be higher; online blitz equalizes this dimension.

2.2 White Advantage by Rating Bracket

Critical finding: White's advantage scales dramatically with rating. At the sub-1200 level, white actually underperforms (35.7%), suggesting beginners do not know how to convert the initiative. By 1500+, white's edge stabilizes at 54%+. At the 2100+ elite level, white wins nearly 3 out of every 4 decisive games (72.3%) — indicating master-level players routinely convert the first-move advantage into a win. This is the largest effect size in the entire study.

2.3 White Win Rate by Time Control

Across the 10 most common time controls, white's win rate clusters tightly around 51–53%, with one notable outlier: 15+10 (55.3%) and 8+0 (53.1%) show the strongest white advantages. Time controls with increment (the "+N" component) tend to favor white slightly more, as increment benefits the player with the initiative who can generate threats without flag concerns.

3. Rating Dynamics and Their Impact on Outcomes

3.1 Rating Distribution

The pooled rating distribution (combining white and black players) centers around a mean of ~1,593 (median 1,565), with a standard deviation of 291 Elo points. The distribution peaks in the 1,400–1,600 range, consistent with Lichess's typical online player base.
